title: 17. Bar Graph, Histogram and Frequency Polygon

q.t: In a histogram the rectangles are drawn:
q.e: The class intervals are continuous, so each bar starts where the last one ends.

q.t: In a bar graph the bars are drawn:
q.e: The bars stand for separate categories, so they are kept apart.

q.t: A frequency polygon is drawn by joining the:
o: Midpoints of the tops of the histogram bars
q.e: Each point is plotted above the class mark at the height of the frequency.

q.t: In a histogram with equal class sizes, the height of a rectangle shows the:
q.e: With equal widths only the height changes.

q.t: In a histogram, the horizontal axis shows the:
q.e: Frequencies go up the vertical axis.

q.t: The x-coordinate of each vertex of a frequency polygon is the:
q.e: The midpoint of the class represents the whole class.

q.t: A zig-zag (kink) near the origin on an axis shows that:
o: The scale does not start from zero
q.e: It warns the reader that part of the axis has been cut out.

q.t: Which graph is best for comparing sales of five different shops?
q.e: Shops are separate categories, not a continuous scale.

q.t: In any histogram, the frequency of a class is proportional to the rectangle’s:
q.e: Area = width × height; with equal widths this reduces to height.

q.t: Which graph is used for a continuous grouped frequency distribution?
q.e: Touching bars show that the classes run on continuously.

q.t: Frequencies: 0–10: 5, 10–20: 8, 20–30: 12, 30–40: 6, 40–50: 4. Which class has the tallest rectangle?
q.e: It has the highest frequency, 12.

q.t: Frequencies: 0–10: 5, 10–20: 8, 20–30: 12, 30–40: 6, 40–50: 4. Find the total frequency.
q.e: Add all the heights.

q.t: Frequencies: 0–10: 5, 10–20: 8, 20–30: 12, 30–40: 6, 40–50: 4. What is the x-coordinate of the first vertex of the frequency polygon (above the first bar)?
q.e: The class mark of 0–10.

q.t: For classes 0–10 to 40–50, the frequency polygon is closed by joining to the class marks of two imaginary classes of zero frequency. One is −5; what is the other?
q.e: The imaginary class after 40–50 is 50–60, with class mark 55.

q.t: Frequencies: 0–10: 5, 10–20: 8, 20–30: 12, 30–40: 6, 40–50: 4. How many rectangles does the histogram have?
q.e: One for each class.

q.t: Frequencies: 0–10: 5, 10–20: 8, 20–30: 12, 30–40: 6, 40–50: 4. How many observations are 30 or more?
Frequencies: 0–10: 5, 10–20: 8, 20–30: 12, 30–40: 6, 40–50: 4. How many observations are less than 20?
With the scale 1 cm = 2 units of frequency, how tall is the rectangle for a frequency of 12 (in cm)?
For classes 0–10, 10–20, …, how wide is each rectangle in units of the x-axis?
q.e: The class size.

q.t: A frequency polygon can be drawn:
o: With or without first drawing a histogram
q.e: Plotting (class mark, frequency) points directly gives the same polygon.

q.t: In a histogram with unequal class sizes, the smallest class size is 10. A class 10–30 has frequency 12. What height should its rectangle have?
q.e: Adjusted height = frequency × (smallest size ÷ class size) = 12 × 10/20, so that area stays proportional to frequency.

q.t: In a histogram with unequal class sizes, the smallest class size is 10. A class 30–60 has frequency 18. What height should its rectangle have?
Before drawing a histogram for classes 10–19, 20–29, 30–39 we must first:
q.e: A histogram has no gaps, so the classes become 9.5–19.5, 19.5–29.5 …

q.t: A histogram has 5 classes. How many vertices does its closed frequency polygon have, counting the two points on the axis?
q.e: One for each class plus the two zero-frequency end points.

q.t: The area enclosed by a frequency polygon and the x-axis, compared with the area of the histogram, is:
q.e: Each small triangle cut off a bar is replaced by a congruent triangle added outside it.

q.t: Frequencies: 0–10: 5, 10–20: 8, 20–30: 12, 30–40: 6, 40–50: 4. What fraction of the observations lie in 20–30?
q.e: 12 out of 35.

q.t: Two frequency polygons are drawn on the same axes in order to:
q.e: Polygons can overlap clearly, which two histograms cannot.

q.t: The class marks of a histogram are 15, 25, 35. What are the boundaries of the first rectangle?
q.e: Class size 10, so 5 either side of 15.

q.t: In a histogram with unequal class sizes, the smallest class size is 5. The class 20–35 is drawn with an adjusted height of 8. What is its actual frequency?
q.e: Adjusted height = frequency × 5/15, so frequency = 8 × 15/5.

q.t: Frequencies: 0–10: 5, 10–20: 8, 20–30: 12, 30–40: 6, 40–50: 4. In which class does the middle (18th) observation lie?
q.e: The first two classes hold 13 and the first three hold 25, so the 18th is in 20–30.

q.t: Classes and frequencies: 0–5: 10, 5–15: 30, 15–30: 45, 30–50: 20. Using the smallest class size (5) as the unit, find the height of the rectangle for 5–15.
Classes and frequencies: 0–5: 10, 5–15: 30, 15–30: 45, 30–50: 20. Find the adjusted height of the rectangle for 15–30.
Classes and frequencies: 0–5: 10, 5–15: 30, 15–30: 45, 30–50: 20. Find the adjusted height of the rectangle for 30–50.
Classes and frequencies: 0–5: 10, 5–15: 30, 15–30: 45, 30–50: 20. Which class has the SHORTEST rectangle after adjusting?
q.e: Heights are 10, 15, 15 and 5 — even though 0–5 has the smallest frequency, it is a narrow class.

q.t: Classes and frequencies: 0–5: 10, 5–15: 30, 15–30: 45, 30–50: 20. Find the total frequency.
q.e: Add the frequencies.

q.t: Classes and frequencies: 0–5: 10, 5–15: 30, 15–30: 45, 30–50: 20. How many observations are below 15?
Classes and frequencies: 0–5: 10, 5–15: 30, 15–30: 45, 30–50: 20. What fraction of the observations are 30 or more?
Classes and frequencies: 0–5: 10, 5–15: 30, 15–30: 45, 30–50: 20. In which class does the middle (53rd) observation lie?
q.e: Cumulative frequencies are 10, 40, 85, 105. The 53rd falls in the third class.

q.t: Two classes have widths 10 and 20 and equal frequencies. In the histogram, the wider class’s rectangle is:
q.e: Equal frequencies need equal areas, so double the width means half the height.

q.t: A histogram of 6 equal classes starts at 100 and ends at 160. What is the class mark of the fourth class?
q.e: Class size 10; the fourth class is 130–140.
